provenance: PeerGrab measurements on the owner's Alibaba Cloud ECS; separate from archived original-project experiments

source.note: The final commit was created after the measurements. The source hashes below identify the measurement tools now in that commit; the ECS-side tool changes were checked against the ECS checkout and matched. External load generators ran on a separate workstation. The application and worker ran from the separately identified container images.

environment.loadTarget: disposable isolated PeerGrab stack with separate MySQL, Redis, RocketMQ and volumes

workloads.request: authenticated first page of published errands, 20 rows from a 10000-row published seed
workloads.interpretation: 700 offered QPS passed a 60-second zero-error round; 720 QPS varied between rounds and 750 QPS showed growing tail latency and no-response errors. This is one read endpoint, not overall business capacity.

workloads.request: authenticated first page of published errands, 20 rows from the same isolated seed
workloads.model: external fixed-arrival HTTP/1.1 via Host Nginx, frontend Nginx and app
workloads.keyResult: 450 offered QPS, 81000/81000 HTTP 200 over 180 seconds, P99 169.4 ms; at 500 offered QPS over 180 seconds, 6 of 90000 requests had no HTTP response
workloads.interpretation: The sustained zero-error observation applies only to this request, seed, path and three-minute window.

workloads.scenario: S2 proxy connection reuse and Hikari/Tomcat ablations
workloads.interpretation: Connection reuse had a repeated full-path A/B/A benefit; single warm-state Hikari/Tomcat rounds do not establish a reliable ranking.

workloads.scenario: S4 settlement and S1 same-task grab spike
workloads.model: finite write batches with database correctness checks
workloads.interpretation: S4 TPS counts durable settlements. S1 spike request count divided by elapsed time is not steady-state QPS.

workloads.model: two finite closed-loop batches of 5000 reads per isolated cache configuration
workloads.interpretation: Closed-loop completion RPS is not a fixed-arrival capacity ceiling.

workloads.scenario: S5 natural expiration by MQ or fallback scan
workloads.model: 1000 and 5000 future-due tasks in separate disposable stacks; latency measured from due time to durable database transition
workloads.interpretation: MQ and scan are different exclusive processing mechanisms, not a single-variable speedup experiment.
